After annotating single-cell subpopulations, the recurring question is how active a pathway is in **each cell or cluster**, and whether two clusters differ \[1\]. GSVA scores every cell for a gene set; the scores are then compared between clusters with a heatmap and a boxplot. This tutorial runs that workflow on a simulated cells × genes matrix — the plotting half of the reference pipeline (matrix → grouping → GSVA → figure).

-   System Requirements: Cross-platform (Linux/MacOS/Windows)

-   Programming Language: R

```{r}
sessioninfo::session_info("attached")
```

## Data Preparation

We simulate log-normalised expression for 400 cells from two endothelial-like subpopulations (EC1, EC2) and six hallmark-like pathways planted with cluster-specific activity — the state right before GSVA in the reference workflow.

```{r load data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
set.seed(1001)
n_cell <- 200                                     # per cluster
genes <- paste0("Gene", sprintf("%04d", 1:300))
cells <- c(paste0("EC1_", sprintf("%03d", 1:n_cell)),
           paste0("EC2_", sprintf("%03d", 1:n_cell)))
cluster <- factor(rep(c("EC1", "EC2"), each = n_cell), levels = c("EC1", "EC2"))

expr <- matrix(rnorm(300 * 2 * n_cell, sd = 0.5), nrow = 300,
               dimnames = list(genes, cells))
pathways <- list(
  "Angiogenesis"       = 1:40,    "EC activation"     = 41:80,
  "Hypoxia"            = 81:110,  "Leukocyte migration" = 111:150,
  "Coagulation"        = 151:180, "Antigen processing"  = 181:210
)
signal <- c(1.4, 1.0, 0.6, -0.3, 0, 0)             # EC1 > EC2 for the first three
for (k in seq_along(pathways)) {
  pg <- names(pathways)[k]
  expr[pathways[[pg]], cluster == "EC1"] <-
    expr[pathways[[pg]], cluster == "EC1"] + signal[k]
}
```

## Visualization

### 1. Per-Cell Pathway Scores (GSVA Heatmap)

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.1GsvaHeatmap
#| fig-cap: "Pathway scores per cell (columns) split by subpopulation; EC1 carries the angiogenesis/activation/hypoxia programs."
#| out.width: "95%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4

## Dependency-free per-cell set score (mean of set genes); the reference
## workflow uses GSVA::gsva() on the normalised matrix — same input, same layout
score_mat <- t(sapply(pathways, function(idx) colMeans(expr[idx, , drop = FALSE])))
score_z <- t(scale(t(score_mat)))

ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(Cluster = cluster,
                        col = list(Cluster = c(EC1 = "#B31E22", EC2 = "#529B40")),
                        show_legend = FALSE)
col_fun <- circlize::colorRamp2(c(-2, 0, 2), c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))
Heatmap(score_z, name = "Score (z)",
        top_annotation = ha, col = col_fun,
        cluster_columns = FALSE,
        column_split = cluster, column_gap = unit(1.5, "mm"),
        row_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 9),
        show_column_names = FALSE, border = TRUE)
```

### 2. Comparing a Pathway Between Clusters

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.2GsvaBox
#| fig-cap: "Angiogenesis scores per cell in EC1 vs EC2; the Wilcoxon p value is annotated."
#| out.width: "60%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 4.5

box_df <- data.frame(cluster = cluster,
                     score = score_mat["Angiogenesis", ])
p_kw <- wilcox.test(score ~ cluster, data = box_df)$p.value

ggplot(box_df, aes(cluster, score, fill = cluster)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.55) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(EC1 = "#B31E22", EC2 = "#529B40")) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Angiogenesis (Wilcoxon %s)",
       ifelse(p_kw < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", p_kw))),
       x = NULL, y = "Pathway score", fill = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

::: callout-tip
**Practice tips**

-   Score cells on the **normalised** data (`GetAssayData(slot = "data")` in Seurat), never raw counts.
-   With real data, run `GSVA::gsva(expr, pathways)` on the cells × genes matrix — the heatmap and boxplot halves stay exactly as here.
-   Two clusters ↔ one Wilcoxon test; for more clusters use a Kruskal-Wallis per pathway (`ggpubr::stat_compare_means(method = "kruskal.test")`).
:::

## Application

Per-cell pathway scoring is the standard read-out when annotating subpopulations (endothelial tips vs phalanx cells, tumour vs stromal fibroblasts). The heatmap reveals which programs define which cluster; the boxplot quantifies one program of interest.
